note.subject: biology
note.title: Specialised cells
note.overview: Relate each specialised cell’s structure to its function and explain differentiation.
learningGoals: Explain the key idea using school examples.
Apply it to a short-answer or calculation question.
mustMemoriseRules: Red blood cells carry oxygen with haemoglobin; biconcave shape aids diffusion and the missing nucleus makes more room.
Neurones transmit impulses along long axons. Muscle cells have contractile proteins and many mitochondria.
Sperm have a tail, an acrosome and mitochondria. Root hair cells have a large surface area.
Palisade cells contain chloroplasts; xylem carries water and phloem moves dissolved sugars.
detailedExplanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen with haemoglobin; biconcave shape aids diffusion and the missing nucleus makes more room.
Neurones transmit impulses along long axons. Muscle cells have contractile proteins and many mitochondria.
Sperm have a tail, an acrosome and mitochondria. Root hair cells have a large surface area.
Palisade cells contain chloroplasts; xylem carries water and phloem moves dissolved sugars.

workedExamples.answer: Feature → effect → function: a root hair increases surface area, increasing absorption from the soil.
workedExamples.why: Follow the units and the biological reason given in the explanation.

commonMistakes: Do not confuse xylem (water) with phloem (sugars).
An adult stem cell has a more limited differentiation range than an embryonic one.
